schema_extension_proposals.affected_entity: sessions.source_ref (+ sessions_source_ref_unique partial unique index on (source, source_ref))
schema_extension_proposals.why_existing_model_insufficient: sessions had no uniqueness constraint at all (noted explicitly in the 0024 migration comment) — a shared-library import had no way to detect 'this WOD is already seeded' short of a full-row comparison, so re-running an import script would append duplicate rows every time.
schema_extension_proposals.additive_change: New nullable text column `source_ref` on sessions (migration 0027), plus a partial unique index on (source, source_ref) WHERE source_ref IS NOT NULL. Imported rows carry a stable per-workout key (e.g. 'benchmark/fran'); the seed migration's INSERT ends with ON CONFLICT (source, source_ref) WHERE source_ref IS NOT NULL DO NOTHING, making a re-apply a no-op.
schema_extension_proposals.backward_compat_impact: Column is nullable and the index is partial (WHERE source_ref IS NOT NULL), so every existing row — legacy strength sessions, user-authored sessions, the 21 Hyrox seed rows from 0024 which have no source_ref — is completely unaffected. No default, no backfill, no RLS change (data-only column, covered by the existing sessions policies).
schema_extension_proposals.consuming_flow: src/lib/queries.ts SessionInput.source_ref / createSession (spreads ...input, so the new optional field passes through unchanged); read by any consumer that reads a Session row (SessionSheet, Sessions library list) but not required by any of them — it is provenance metadata, not part of the Logger's runtime path.

schema_extension_proposals.affected_entity: SessionFrame.variants (SessionVariant[]) in src/lib/types.ts; consumed by src/lib/logBuilder.ts buildLogFromSession/selectVariant/availableLevels
schema_extension_proposals.why_existing_model_insufficient: The existing frame shape (flat `exercises[]` plus optional `groups[]`) can express a single prescription only. CrossFit benchmark WODs are conventionally published with three parallel scaled prescriptions (Rx / Intermediate / Beginner) sharing one scoring format and one circuit structure but different loads/movement substitutions — there was no way to store more than one prescription per session without either duplicating the whole session row per level (losing the 'same WOD, three scales' relationship) or overloading `notes` with unstructured scaling text the Logger could not act on.
schema_extension_proposals.additive_change: New optional `variants?: SessionVariant[]` array on SessionFrame. Each SessionVariant is {level: 'rx'|'intermediate'|'beginner', label?, groups: SessionGroup[], timeCapSeconds?, instructions?} — reusing the existing SessionGroup/SessionExercise shapes, so no new nested contract was invented. Stored inside the existing `frame` JSONB column; no new SQL column. `selectVariant`/`availableLevels`/`buildLogFromSession(frame, level?)` in logBuilder.ts implement the selection and fallback (requested level -> rx -> first) and the unfold-to-LogDocument path.
schema_extension_proposals.backward_compat_impact: `variants` is optional. Every pre-existing frame (Hyrox seed rows from 0024, all user-authored sessions, plan-derived frames) has no `variants` key and is untouched; buildLogFromSession falls through unchanged to `frame.groups` then `frame.exercises` exactly as before. When `variants` IS present, the top-level `exercises`/`groups` are kept as the Rx mirror specifically so old readers that don't know about `variants` still see a coherent single-prescription frame.
schema_extension_proposals.consuming_flow: src/lib/logBuilder.ts (buildLogFromSession, selectVariant, availableLevels) is the only backend-side consumer today. The scaling-level picker UI (a SessionSheet control passing the chosen ScalingLevel into buildLogFromSession before calling queries.createLog) is a UI-side addition outside this task's scope — flagging that the Logger/SessionSheet UI needs to surface availableLevels() as a Rx/Intermediate/Beginner toggle for this to reach the user; the data and selection logic are done, the toggle affordance is not part of this backend change.

source_note: Two seed migrations back this output. supabase/migrations/0028_seed_crossfit.sql seeds the 8 canonical benchmark WODs mapped in full below (source='CrossFit.com', source_ref='benchmark/<slug>'). supabase/migrations/0029_seed_crossfit_daily.sql seeds 22 additional real, dated daily WODs (source_ref='daily/YYMMDD', Jul 4 - Aug 3, 2026) captured via browser inspection of crossfit.com/workout (server-side fetch returns 403). Per the source-filtering rule, 9 rest-day / pure-editorial dates in the same capture were excluded outright — no session, no placeholder, no empty log was created for them: 2026-07-05, 07-09, 07-12, 07-16, 07-19, 07-23, 07-26, 07-30, 08-02. The full session frame JSON for the 22 daily WODs is authoritative in the migration SQL (each frame is large — up to 3 scaling variants × several movements); this file carries a compact summary plus the accompanying deduplication_actions and the movements these WODs required.
